projects.name: Sig Sauer MCX
projects.pitch: A CAD-to-game weapon asset, modeled in Fusion 360 and presented in Unreal Engine.
projects.description: A 3D recreation of the SIG Sauer MCX, developed to explore a workflow combining CAD modeling with a modern real-time game asset pipeline. The modeling process started in Fusion 360, which allowed me to build the weapon using precise mechanical forms and clean hard-surface geometry. The model was then transferred to Autodesk 3ds Max, where the optimized low-poly version was created and prepared for baking. Additional surface adjustments and small imperfections were introduced in ZBrush to reduce the overly perfect CAD appearance and add subtle realism. The baking process was handled in Marmoset Toolbag, generating the maps required for the texturing stage. The materials were then created in Substance 3D Painter, focusing on realistic metal surfaces, wear, and manufacturing details. The final asset was imported into Unreal Engine, where the lighting and real-time rendering were used to present the final result.

projects.name: EOTech EXPS3
projects.pitch: A game-ready recreation of the EOTech EXPS3 holographic sight.
projects.description: A highly detailed recreation of the EOTech EXPS3 holographic sight, one of the most iconic optics used by military and law enforcement worldwide. The project focused on capturing the precision engineering of the real unit — from the distinctive hood geometry and adjustment turrets to the battery compartment and quick-detach lever. Every surface detail was carefully modeled, including the subtle casting textures, laser-engraved markings, and the internal holographic reticle housing. The texturing phase emphasized the contrast between the matte anodized aluminum body, polished lens coatings, and worn rubber accents, resulting in a production-ready game asset that balances visual fidelity with optimized geometry.

projects.name: PMAG x NATO Cartridge
projects.pitch: A material study of polymer, brass, copper and steel under controlled studio light.
projects.description: A detailed study of the Magpul PMAG 30-round magazine paired with a NATO 5.56×45mm cartridge. This project was born from the desire to push material accuracy on seemingly simple objects — exploring how polymer, brass, copper, and steel all interact under controlled lighting. The PMAG was modeled in Fusion 360 to capture the precise injection-molded geometry, ribbed grip texture, and anti-tilt follower mechanism. The cartridge was built with attention to the primer pocket, case mouth crimp, and boat-tail bullet profile. Texturing in Substance Painter focused on micro-surface variation: the matte polymer with subtle mold flow lines, fingerprint smudges on brass casings, and the cold shimmer of a jacketed bullet tip. The final renders were composed in Marmoset Toolbag to highlight material separation and form language.

projects.name: PPSH-41
projects.pitch: A game-ready recreation of the WW2 Soviet submachine gun, built on a 50K triangle budget.
projects.description: A detailed recreation of the PPSh-41, the iconic Soviet submachine gun that became one of the most recognizable weapons of the Second World War. The project focused on capturing the weapon's distinctive silhouette — the ventilated barrel shroud, the drum magazine housing, and the wooden stock — while adhering to game-ready production constraints. The model was built in 3ds Max, combining high-poly sculpted details with an optimized low-poly base of 50K triangles total. A single 4K PBR material covers the entire weapon, with dedicated 2K materials for each magazine. Texturing in Substance Painter emphasized the contrast between the blued steel barrel, worn wooden grip, and the cold matte finish of the drum magazine — with particular attention to period-accurate wear patterns, oil stains, and impact marks that give the asset its historical character. Final presentation was composed in Marmoset Toolbag using volumetric lighting to reinforce the atmospheric quality of the piece.

specs.Textures: One 4K PBR set for the weapon, one 2K set per magazine
